basis: August 8, 2023 is the earliest qualifying communication I could verify. Diodes reported consolidated GAAP net sales of $467,152,000 for Q2 2023 versus $500,972,000 for Q2 2022, below the $475,923,400 cutoff. The May 9 guidance high was $481,010,000. The earliest date remains unresolved because I could verify two intervening management fireside chats but could not verify their remarks from a primary transcript or replay.

coverage.detail: The February 6 Q4 2022 release forecast $467 million ±3% specifically for Q1 2023.
The February 6 earnings-call transcript likewise assigned the forecast to Q1. I found no numeric Q2 consolidated revenue ceiling in the call.
The May 9 Q1 release explicitly forecast Q2 2023 revenue of $467 million ±3%. The high end exceeded the cutoff by $5,086,600.
Slide 15 repeated the May 9 Q2 range of $467 million ±3%.
Slide 32 of the second presentation gave the same Q2 range and explicitly dated it May 9.
On the May 9 public call, the CFO repeated $467 million ±3% for Q2 and described flat sequential revenue as the midpoint. The transcript was furnished May 16.

Diodes announced May 31 Mizuho meetings, a June 1 TD Cowen fireside chat with a public webcast, and a June 6 Baird fireside chat. The announcement contained no sales update. I could not verify the TD Cowen remarks.
Diodes’ event page confirms the June 6 Baird session at 2 p.m. EDT and says the webcast is unavailable. I found no primary transcript to check for a narrower Q2 outlook.
The July 18 notice scheduled the August 8 results release and conference call. It gave no preliminary sales figure or revised outlook.

The August 8 release’s consolidated statements of operations show net sales, in thousands, of 467,152 and 500,972 in the respective three-month columns for June 2023 and June 2022. The release reports a 6.8% year-over-year decline.

publication_date_evidence: Diodes’ results release carries an August 8, 2023 Plano dateline and announces results that day for the quarter ended June 30. This establishes the public date of the actuals. The June conference coverage gap prevents certifying it as the first qualifying communication.
